findings.body: The conversion `u32::try_from(round.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)` saturates at `u32::MAX` when the vector length exceeds 2^32, but `round.len()` is `usize` on a 64-bit platform and a round of 4 billion+ turns would break the counting logic. The diff comment "non-empty, in desk order, and bounded by two separate widths" (from the `HiveStep::Speak` definition) guarantees the length is at most `policy.round_width` or `policy.revealed_width`, which are `u32` in the episode policy — well under `u32::MAX`. The `unwrap_or` is a dead branch that saturates silently; a `unwrap` with a clarifying comment would be honest about the invariant.
findings.suggestion:
let round_len = u32::try_from(round.len()).unwrap();
// round.len() is bounded by policy.round_width or policy.revealed_width, both u32
findings.title: Guard round_len calculation against overflow

value.summary: The change generalizes the host loop from single-turn steps to multi-turn rounds. Each round's turns are appended to the journal before the state is committed, and the pinboard read uses `turn.round_start` as its exclusive bound to match the transcript projection. The logic is sound for the code shown and looks ready to merge after verifying the handling of `round_len` for overflow when the input vector exceeds `u32::MAX` (an unreachable input in practice).
